overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated Shorts reveals a distinct performance divide: first-person hypothetical survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme exoplanetary conditions drive peak reach (800-1,000+ views) and highest engagement (likes-to-view ratio >3.5% and active comments). In contrast, generic psychology brain facts ('Fake Memories', 'Earworms') and short animal trivia ('Octopus hearts', 'Sharks vs trees') stall between 10 and 200 views. Pacing data also shows 19-21s durations strongly outperform 12-16s clips.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Extreme Cosmic Survival ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Liquid Diamond Planet' generated 1,029 views and channel-high 38 likes; 'Planet of Burning Ice' reached 972 views; 'Darkest Planet' pulled 823 views.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor scripts around high-stakes second-person POV ('You step out of your capsule...') confronting surreal cosmic environments.

winning_patterns.pattern: 21-Second Narrative Pacing with Tactile Atmospheric Horrors
winning_patterns.evidence: Top 5 non-outlier performers average 20.6 seconds in length, retaining viewers through multi-stage physical escalation rather than rapid 12s single-fact trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Set runtime target strictly to 20-21 seconds, structured into a 3-act descent: arrival, atmospheric hazard, and deadly terminal twist.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined across multiple attempts (5, 10, and 53 views); 'Songs Stuck in Your Head' achieved only 17 to 71 views.
weak_patterns.action: Deprecate routine neuro-trivia unless tied to cinematic horror or visceral survival stakes.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'This Star Is Older Than the Universe' garnered only 11 views; 'Star Colder Than Ice' plateaued at 83 views.
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate static declarative titles; reframe celestial anomalies through active danger or impossible sensory paradoxes.
